did_you_know.text: Did you know? Malachi opens chapter 2 with a direct command to the priests, emphasizing that they must listen to the word of the LORD and honor his name.
Did you know? The LORD warns the priests that if they do not take his name’s honor to heart, he will turn their blessings into curses.

Did you know? To describe the severity of the punishment, the prophet uses a striking image: the LORD will rebuke their offspring, spread dung on the faces of the priests, and carry them away with it.
Did you know? The covenant with Levi is described as a covenant of life and peace, given to Levi along with reverence and fear of the LORD.

Did you know? The proper model for a priest is someone who has true instruction in his mouth, whose lips speak no injustice, who walks with the LORD in peace and uprightness, and who helps many turn away from sin.

Did you know? According to Malachi, a priest’s lips should preserve knowledge, and the people should seek instruction from his mouth; therefore, the priest is called “the messenger of the LORD of hosts.”
Did you know? The prophet accuses the priests of turning from the way, causing many to stumble through their teaching, and corrupting the covenant with Levi.

Did you know? Malachi grounds brotherhood in Israel in the fact that everyone has one Father and one God, and from this he condemns betrayal of one’s brother and profaning the covenant of the ancestors.

Did you know? Marriage is presented here as a covenant: the woman is called “your companion” and “the wife of your covenant,” and betraying the wife of one’s youth is portrayed as violating the LORD’s testimony.
Did you know? The chapter ends with a rebuke of a distorted moral claim: people say that those who do evil are good in the eyes of the LORD, and they even ask, “Where is the God of justice?”
